payload.claim: This case (and every case in `test_a_lens_named_unreviewed_gets_no_verdict_session_and_keeps_its_numbers`) cannot distinguish `_guarded_blockers(numbered, acceptance)` (saffron/phases/rebut.py:1046, called with the full, unfiltered `numbered`) from the spec's listed wrong version 'The guard is read over the numbering with the named lenses' blockers dropped.' `_guarded_blockers` computes its dict entry-by-entry, independent of which other entries are present (saffron/phases/rebut.py:584-608), and `_check_withdrawal_refusals` only ever consults the entry for a blocker that actually produced a `Verdict`, i.e. one whose lens is not in `unreviewed`. So for every case this test builds, the guarded blocker's own lens is never the one named in `unreviewed`, and dropping some other, unguarded blocker from the list passed to `_guarded_blockers` has no observable effect on `result.verdicts`. The task's own in-cell rebuttal record for this exact wrong version argues precisely this ('the finding is real only as an internal contract, not a black-box one') and claims the fix was 'a spy on rebut._guarded_blockers that records the length of its first argument' — but no such spy, or any other internal-contract check, exists anywhere in this diff or the current tests/test_rebut.py. This breaks CLAUDE.md's stated convention, 'A new test is not trusted until it runs against the unfixed code. A test guarding a property already true runs against an edit that breaks it': the witness that is supposed to fail against this wrong version does not, so criterion 3's acceptance ('rebut.run_rebut takes a keyword unreviewed...') is not actually guarded against it despite being listed as a required wrong_versions check.
